Pre-set formations, 4 deployment zones,.DESCRIPTION: Before launching a raid the attacker enters a Planning Phase. Here they view the enemy base layout (based on Intel Center level), assign units to deployment zones, arrange custom grid formations, and confirm the attack. No changes can be made once the raid launches.

The map has 4 deployment zones - North, South, East, West - one on each side of the enemy base. Attacker distributes their army across any combination of zones. Each zone can hold units up to its capacity. Splitting forces creates multi-front pressure but thins each wave.

Within each deployment zone the attacker arranges units on a formation grid before launch. The grid is typically 5 columns wide. Unit placement determines attack order - front row units engage first, rear row units follow. Players can place any mix of unit classes in any position.

Once confirmed all units advance simultaneously from their deployment zones toward the enemy base. Units follow pathfinding AI toward target priority buildings. The 3-minute countdown begins the moment the first unit crosses the base perimeter.

Ground units advance and attack based on their Target Priority stat - Defenses, Resources, or Buildings. Units pathfind around walls until a breach is made. Heavy Tanks and SPGs can breach walls directly. Units engage defenses that fire on them.

When 50% of deployed ground units are destroyed the air units automatically launch from all active deployment zones simultaneously. This is the second wave. Air units fly over walls and defenses ignoring ground obstacles. Fighters engage AA towers first. Attack aircraft and helicopters hit buildings and armor.

3 minutes from first perimeter breach. When time expires all surviving units are recalled. Destruction percentage at time of expiry determines outcome. A well-planned attack should be able to reach 75-100% destruction in 3 minutes if formations and zones are chosen correctly.

Players can manually trigger retreat at any point during the raid. Surviving units return to their deployment zones and the raid ends immediately. Outcome is calculated on destruction at time of retreat. Retreating early preserves Oil since surviving units cost less to redeploy.

The defending base fights back automatically using all placed defense towers and the War Bunker garrison. The defender is not present during the raid. Defense towers fire on the nearest valid target within range automatically. Mines trigger on contact. The EW Jamming Tower affects all incoming guided units.

After the raid ends both attacker and defender see a full summary: destruction percentage, buildings destroyed, resources stolen, Oil spent, trophies gained or lost, and a replay option. The attacker can watch a full replay of the raid from any deployment zone angle.

GRID RULES.col1: North and South zones: 5 columns x 4 rows (20 slots). East and West zones: 4 columns x 3 rows (12 slots). Each slot holds one unit.
Row 1 (front) advances first and takes initial fire. Row 2 advances when Row 1 reaches the wall. Rows 3 and 4 follow sequentially. Rear rows are shielded by front rows.
Units in the same row advance side by side. Column position determines which part of the base each unit targets - left column targets left side defenses, right column targets right side.
Only one unit per grid slot. Housing cost still applies - a Heavy Tank costs more housing so fewer fit in the same formation than Light Tanks.
Once the raid launches the formation is locked. Units follow their programmed path. No changes mid-raid except the retreat command.
Air units placed in the formation grid do NOT deploy at raid start. Their grid position determines launch order when the 50% loss trigger fires. Front row air units launch first.
Empty slots are valid. A sparse formation with wide spacing reduces splash damage taken from Mortar and Bomb towers.
Players can save up to 5 named formation templates per deployment zone. Reuse successful formations without rebuilding from scratch each raid.

Lights move fast and split defender attention. Pack the flanks for speed raids.
SPGs fire over allies hitting buildings and defenses behind walls from safety.

A typical 3-minute raid broken into phas.What Happens: Player views enemy base. Assigns units to zones. Arranges formation grids. Reviews Intel Center data on enemy resources and defenses. Confirms attack.
Units appear in their deployment zones in formation order. Countdown begins. No changes possible.
All units advance from all active zones simultaneously. Light and Fast units reach outer perimeter first. Heavy Tanks and SPGs follow.
Lead units reach outer wall or first mines. Mines detonate on contact. Heavy Tanks begin wall breach. TDs open fire at max range. Defenses begin engaging.
First wall sections breached. Ground units begin flooding through gaps. Defenses pivot to new threats. Mortar towers begin splash fire on clusters.
Main engagement. Ground units fighting across the base. Defenses taking damage. Resources being stolen by Light Tanks. SPGs lobbing shells from rear.
When half the deployed ground units are destroyed all air units launch simultaneously from their zones. Fighters arrive first clearing AA. Attack aircraft follow.
Full air assault underway. Fighters suppressing CIWS and SAM. Helicopters engaging armor. Ground Attack strafing buildings. Bombers on high-value targets.
Combined arms assault. Surviving ground plus full air wave pushing through remaining defenses. Command Center targeted if not already destroyed.
All surviving units recalled to deployment zones. Raid ends. Destruction percentage calculated. Resources stolen confirmed. Trophies adjusted.
Summary screen shown to attacker. Defender notified of attack with full replay. Shield applied to defender. Resources deducted from defender storage.
